Spain's Melting Pot Has a Very Selective Simmer

Thousands of migrants swam or climbed the fence into Ceuta on Thursday, Spain's six-mile foothold on Morocco's coast, forcing Madrid to mobilize its military just to hold the line. 

At least 18 people died trying to make the crossing. Ceuta's president, Juan Jesús Vivas, called it "a situation of total humanitarian and social emergency." The Ceuta government went further, describing an "unprecedented situation that is testing our institutional response capacity."

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has spent years marketing Spain as the West's alternative to nativist Europe, rolling out the welcome mat for Latin American migrants who share the language and the religion. 

Thursday tested how far that welcome actually extends. His response to tens of thousands of mostly young African men walking onto Spanish soil was a written pledge that the government is "fully committed to providing an immediate response," followed immediately by tanks, drones, and naval patrols. The melting pot, it turns out, comes with a border fence and an asterisk.

The right wasted no time turning tragedy into a campaign ad. Vox leader Santiago Abascal declared "This is an invasion," while Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the situation "desperate" and accused the government of shirking responsibility, without offering an alternative that doesn't also end in troops on a beach. 

Spain's own interior ministry blames smuggling networks exploiting a Supreme Court ruling that bars summarily returning migrants intercepted at sea, a legal detail nobody on television seems interested in mentioning. 

Meanwhile the EU's response to a member state facing an actual emergency was a tweet from Commissioner Magnus Brunner offering Frontex support and reassuring everyone that "the protection of the Union's external borders is a crucial part of our efforts."

So the progressive government sends the army, the far right calls it an invasion, and Brussels sends a statement. Eighteen people are already dead, and somehow every faction still comes out of this insisting it was right all along, about people who never got a vote in any of it.

📣 Brazil stablecoins face IMF scrutiny as crypto flows outpace capital 

🌐 IMF has called for closer oversight of Brazil’s stablecoin market as cross-border crypto flows outpace traditional capital movements. The report says cross-border crypto transactions have increased faster than conventional capital flows and now require closer regulatory attention because of their growing links with the country’s financial system. The assessment says stablecoin purchases respond much more strongly to global financial shocks than traditional portfolio investment or foreign direct investment. 

🔔 Based on the IMF’s analysis, purchases of dollar-backed stablecoins are two to three times more sensitive to external market events, raising concerns over how quickly international volatility could spread through crypto markets. Brazil has emerged as one of the world’s more active crypto markets, with stablecoins accounting for a significant share of digital asset activity. The IMF said the country’s crypto ecosystem has become increasingly connected with the traditional financial sector, making regulatory oversight more important as adoption continues to rise.

⚠️ The report acknowledges that Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) has already introduced measures to regulate crypto asset service providers. Even so, the IMF said several areas still need stronger rules, including customer asset protection, stablecoin issuance requirements, and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) standards.
